questions.question: A solution in which no more solute can be dissolved at the same temperature and pressure is called a:
questions.explanation: A saturated solution is in dynamic thermodynamic equilibrium with undissolved solute, meaning no additional solute can dissolve at that specified temperature.

questions.sub_topic: Henry's Law Constant and Gas Solubility
questions.question: For different gases dissolved in water at the same temperature, higher value of Henry's law constant (\( K_H \)) indicates:
options: A) Higher solubility of the gas in water
B) Lower solubility of the gas in water
C) Zero partial pressure above the liquid
D) Higher boiling point of the solution
questions.explanation: From Henry's law \( p = K_H \chi \), at a given partial pressure \( p \), \( \chi = p / K_H \). Hence, higher \( K_H \) corresponds to a smaller mole fraction (lower solubility).

questions.sub_topic: Depression of Freezing Point of Camphor (Rast Method)
questions.question: Camphor is frequently used as a solvent in the Rast micro-method for determining molecular mass because:
options: A) It boils below room temperature
B) It forms a completely ionic solution with organic solutes
C) Its freezing point is unaffected by impurities
D) It has an exceptionally large molal depression constant (\( K_f \approx 40 \text{ K kg mol}^{-1} \))
questions.explanation: Camphor's very high cryoscopic constant (\( K_f \approx 39.7-40.0 \text{ K kg/mol} \)) gives a large, easily measurable freezing point depression even for tiny amounts of solute.

questions.question: An aqueous solution of glucose is 2.0 M and has a density of 1.12 g/mL. What is the molality of this solution? (Molar mass of glucose = 180 g/mol)
questions.explanation: Mass of 1 L solution = \( 1000 \times 1.12 = 1120 \text{ g} \). Mass of glucose = \( 2.0 \times 180 = 360 \text{ g} \). Mass of solvent (water) = \( 1120 - 360 = 760 \text{ g} = 0.76 \text{ kg} \). Molality \( m = \frac{2.0}{0.76} \approx 2.63 \text{ mol/kg} \).

questions.sub_topic: Van't Hoff Factor for Potassium Ferricyanide
questions.question: Assuming 80% dissociation (\( \alpha = 0.80 \)), what is the Van't Hoff factor (\( i \)) for potassium ferricyanide, \( \ce{K3[Fe(CN)6]} \)?
The cell constant (\( G^* \)) of a conductivity cell is defined as the ratio of:
options: A) Cross-sectional area (\( A \)) to distance between electrodes (\( l \))
B) Distance between electrodes (\( l \)) to their cross-sectional area (\( A \))
C) Resistance (\( R \)) to specific conductance (\( \kappa \))
D) Molar conductivity to limiting molar conductivity
questions.explanation: Cell constant \( G^* = l/A \), determined experimentally by measuring the resistance of a standard \( \ce{KCl} \) solution whose conductivity is precisely known.

questions.sub_topic: Fuel Cell Efficiency vs Thermal Power Plants
questions.question: Hydrogen-oxygen fuel cells offer an electrical thermodynamic efficiency of ~70%, which is significantly higher than conventional thermal power plants (~40%), because:
options: A) They operate at temperatures near absolute zero
B) They consume heavy radioactive water as coolant
C) They convert chemical free energy directly into electrical energy without Carnot cycle heat-engine limitations
D) They produce zero entropy under all operating conditions
questions.explanation: Fuel cells convert Gibbs free energy change (\( \Delta G \)) directly into electricity without intermediate conversion to heat and mechanical work, bypassing Carnot thermodynamic efficiency limits.

questions.question: In the electrochemical mechanism of rusting of iron, the reduction occurring at the cathodic site in the presence of acidic moisture is:
questions.explanation: At the anodic site: \( \ce{Fe -> Fe^{2+} + 2e^-} \). Electrons travel through the metal to another spot where \( \ce{H+} \) (from dissolved \( \ce{CO2} \)) facilitates reduction of \( \ce{O2} \) to \( \ce{H2O} \).

questions.question: For a galvanic cell reaction with \( n=2 \) at 298 K, if the standard cell potential is \( E^\circ_{\text{cell}} = 0.2955 \text{ V} \), the equilibrium constant \( K_c \) is:

questions.sub_topic: Molar Conductivity of Saturated Salt Solution
questions.question: The conductivity of a saturated solution of \( \ce{AgCl} \) at 298 K is \( 1.382 \times 10^{-6} \text{ S cm}^{-1} \) after subtracting that of water. If \( \Lambda_m^\circ(\ce{AgCl}) = 138.2 \text{ S cm}^2 \text{mol}^{-1} \), what is the solubility product (\( K_{sp} \)) of \( \ce{AgCl} \)?
questions.explanation: Solubility \( S = \frac{\kappa \times 1000}{\Lambda_m^\circ} = \frac{1.382 \times 10^{-6} \times 1000}{138.2} = 1.0 \times 10^{-5} \text{ mol/L} \). \( K_{sp} = S^2 = (1.0 \times 10^{-5})^2 = 1.0 \times 10^{-10} \).

questions.question: A chemical reaction that takes place in a single microscopic step without forming any detectable intermediates is called an:
questions.explanation: An elementary reaction is a single-step reaction where reactants collide and form products directly in one transition state.

questions.sub_topic: Zero Order Reaction Concentration vs Time Plot
questions.question: For a zero-order reaction \( \ce{A -> Products} \), a plot of reactant concentration \( [A] \) versus time \( t \) gives a straight line with:
questions.explanation: From the integrated rate equation \( [A] = -kt + [A]_0 \), comparing with \( y = mx + c \) gives slope \( m = -k \) and y-intercept \( c = [A]_0 \).

questions.sub_topic: Effect of Temperature on Rate Constant: Arrhenius Fraction
questions.question: In the Arrhenius equation \( k = A e^{-E_a / (RT)} \), if the temperature approaches infinity (\( T \to \infty \)), the rate constant \( k \) approaches:
questions.explanation: As \( T \to \infty \), \( \frac{E_a}{RT} \to 0 \), so \( e^{-E_a/(RT)} \to e^0 = 1 \), and \( k \to A \).

questions.sub_topic: Time for 99.9% Completion in First Order
questions.question: For a first-order reaction, the time required for 99.9% completion (\( t_{99.9\%} \)) is approximately how many times its half-life (\( t_{1/2} \))?

For a first-order gas-phase decomposition \( \ce{A(g) -> B(g) + C(g)} \), let initial pressure of A be \( p_i \) and total pressure at time \( t \) be \( p_t \). The rate constant \( k \) is given by:
questions.explanation: At time \( t \), \( p_A = p_i - x \), \( p_B = x \), \( p_C = x \). Total \( p_t = p_i + x \Rightarrow x = p_t - p_i \). Thus \( p_A = p_i - (p_t - p_i) = 2p_i - p_t \). Therefore, \( k = \frac{2.303}{t} \log \frac{p_i}{2p_i - p_t} \).

questions.topic: Unit IV: d and f Block Elements
questions.question: Which of the following 3d transition metals exhibits ferromagnetism at room temperature?
questions.explanation: Iron, cobalt, and nickel are ferromagnetic substances that possess spontaneous permanent magnetic moments due to aligned domains at room temperature.

questions.topic: Unit IV: d and f Block Elements
questions.question: The standard reduction potential \( E^\circ_{\ce{Mn^{3+}/Mn^{2+}}} = +1.57 \text{ V} \) is much higher than \( E^\circ_{\ce{Fe^{3+}/Fe^{2+}}} = +0.77 \text{ V} \). This indicates that:
options: A) \( \ce{Mn^{2+}} \) readily oxidizes to \( \ce{Mn^{3+}} \) in air
B) \( \ce{Mn^{3+}} \) is a strong oxidizing agent because reduction to \( \ce{Mn^{2+}} \) produces a stable half-filled \( 3d^5 \) configuration
C) Iron(III) is less stable than manganese(III)
D) Manganese has lower electronegativity than iron
questions.explanation: \( \ce{Mn^{3+}} \) (\( 3d^4 \)) readily gains an electron to form \( \ce{Mn^{2+}} \) (\( 3d^5 \)), which has an exceptionally stable half-filled d-subshell, making \( \ce{Mn^{3+}} \) a strong oxidant.

questions.topic: Unit IV: d and f Block Elements
questions.question: Europium exhibits a stable +2 oxidation state and terbium exhibits a stable +4 oxidation state because:
options: A) Both ions have empty 4f subshells
B) Both ions have completely filled \( 4f^{14} \) subshells
C) Both ions form stable diatomic gases
D) Both ions achieve the extra stability of a half-filled \( 4f^7 \) electronic configuration
questions.explanation: \( \ce{Eu^{2+}} \) has configuration \( [\ce{Xe}] 4f^7 \) and \( \ce{Tb^{4+}} \) has configuration \( [\ce{Xe}] 4f^7 \); both attain the special stability of a half-filled 4f subshell.

questions.topic: Unit IV: d and f Block Elements
questions.question: Separation of individual lanthanoid elements from each other is difficult chemically, but accomplished effectively by ion-exchange chromatography because:
options: A) Lanthanoids have drastically different boiling points
B) Slight differences in ionic size cause small differences in the stability constants of their complex formation with chelating agents
C) Some lanthanoids are completely insoluble in water
D) Lanthanoids have completely different chemical valence states
questions.explanation: Because of lanthanoid contraction, ionic radii decrease systematically from \( \ce{La^{3+}} \) to \( \ce{Lu^{3+}} \), leading to gradual variations in complex stability with ligands like citrate or EDTA.

questions.topic: Unit IV: d and f Block Elements
questions.sub_topic: Potassium Dichromate Reaction with Hydrogen Sulfide
questions.question: When \( \ce{H2S} \) gas is passed through an acidified solution of potassium dichromate, the orange solution turns green with turbidity due to:
options: A) Formation of black chromium sulfide precipitate
B) Reduction of dichromate to green \( \ce{Cr^{3+}} \) and oxidation of \( \ce{H2S} \) to colloidal sulfur
C) Complete decomposition of water into hydrogen gas
D) Formation of green chromate ions without sulfur
questions.explanation: \( \ce{Cr2O7^{2-} + 8H+ + 3H2S -> 2Cr^{3+}(green) + 3S(colloidal) + 7H2O} \). Acidified dichromate oxidizes sulfide to elemental sulfur.

questions.sub_topic: Primary Valency of Metal in Coordination Compound
questions.question: In the coordination compound \( [\ce{Co(NH3)4Cl2}]\ce{Cl} \), what is the primary valency of the cobalt ion?
questions.explanation: Primary valency corresponds to the oxidation state of the metal: \( x + 4(0) + 2(-1) + (-1) = 0 \Rightarrow x = +3 \).

questions.question: The correct IUPAC name of the complex \( \ce{K3[Fe(C2O4)3]} \) is:
questions.explanation: Cation is potassium; anion has three bidentate oxalate ligands (trioxalato) and iron in oxidation state +3 (3 - 6 = -3), so the name is potassium trioxalatoferrate(III).

questions.question: Octahedral complexes of copper(II) (\( d^9 \), e.g. \( [\ce{Cu(H2O)6}]^{2+} \)) frequently show tetragonal distortion (elongation along the z-axis) due to:
options: A) Coordination of water molecules via hydrogen atoms
B) Jahn-Teller effect caused by unequal electron occupancy of degenerate \( e_g \) orbitals
C) Loss of all unpaired electrons in copper
D) Strong magnetic repulsion from counter ions
questions.explanation: In an octahedral \( d^9 \) complex, the \( e_g \) set has configuration \( (d_{z^2})^2 (d_{x^2-y^2})^1 \) or vice versa. This electronic degeneracy lifts via tetragonal elongation (Jahn-Teller theorem).

questions.sub_topic: Crystal Field Splitting in Tetrahedral Field
questions.question: In tetrahedral crystal field splitting, the five d-orbitals split into two sets, where the orbitals having higher energy are:
options: C) \( t_{2g} \) set with an inversion center
D) All five orbitals remain degenerate
questions.explanation: In a tetrahedral complex, the four ligands approach between the axes, pointing closer to \( d_{xy}, d_{yz}, d_{xz} \) (designated \( t_2 \)), raising them to higher energy than \( d_{x^2-y^2}, d_{z^2} \) (\( e \)).

questions.question: What is the total number of stereoisomers (geometrical plus optical) possible for the octahedral complex \( [\ce{Co(en)2Cl2}]^+ \)?
options: A) 2 (cis and trans only, neither is chiral)
B) 4 (both cis and trans have enantiomers)
D) 3 (trans-isomer is achiral, while cis-isomer exists as a pair of enantiomers)
questions.explanation: The trans isomer has a plane of symmetry and is optically inactive. The cis isomer is chiral and exists as non-superimposable dextro and laevo enantiomers, giving 3 stereoisomers in total.

questions.sub_topic: Order of Boiling Points of Haloalkanes
questions.question: For a given alkyl group \( \ce{R} \), the boiling points of alkyl halides decrease in the order:
questions.explanation: As the halogen atom increases in size and mass from F to I, polarizability increases, resulting in stronger London dispersion and van der Waals forces: \( \ce{RI > RBr > RCl > RF} \).

questions.sub_topic: Reactivity of Haloalkanes with Aqueous vs Alcoholic KOH
questions.question: When 1-bromobutane is treated with aqueous \( \ce{KOH} \), the primary reaction that occurs is:
options: B) Oxidation to form butanoic acid
D) Nucleophilic substitution to form butan-1-ol
questions.explanation: Aqueous \( \ce{KOH} \) provides hydrated hydroxide ions (\( \ce{OH^-} \)) which act primarily as a nucleophile rather than a base, yielding substitution product butan-1-ol via \( \text{S}_\text{N}2 \).

questions.sub_topic: Stereochemistry of SN1 Mechanism with Secondary Halide
questions.question: Hydrolysis of optically active 2-bromobutane in aqueous acetone under conditions favoring \( \text{S}_\text{N}1 \) results in:
options: A) 100% complete retention of optical configuration
B) 100% complete inversion of optical configuration
C) Partial racemization with an excess of inverted product
D) An optically pure meso diastereomer
questions.explanation: In \( \text{S}_\text{N}1 \), the leaving group departs to form a planar carbocation, but the bromide ion shields the front face initially, resulting in racemization with partial net inversion.

questions.question: Heating alkyl halides with zinc metal in dry ether gives dialkylzinc (Frankland reagent), which upon heating with another alkyl halide yields:
options: A) A symmetrical or unsymmetrical alkane
questions.explanation: The Frankland reaction uses organozinc compounds (\( \ce{R2Zn} \)) to couple alkyl halides and produce higher alkanes: \( \ce{R2Zn + 2R'X -> 2R-R' + ZnX2} \).

questions.sub_topic: Dow's Process for Phenol from Chlorobenzene
questions.question: In Dow's commercial process, chlorobenzene is converted into phenol by heating with aqueous \( \ce{NaOH} \) under drastic conditions of:
options: B) 373 K in concentrated nitric acid
C) 623 K and 300 atm pressure followed by acidification
D) 500 K in liquid anhydrous ammonia
questions.explanation: Because the aryl C-Cl bond possesses partial double bond character due to resonance, nucleophilic substitution requires extreme conditions (623 K and 300 atm in aqueous \( \ce{NaOH} \)) to yield sodium phenoxide, which upon acidification gives phenol.

questions.topic: Unit VII: Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers
questions.question: Commercial ethanol is denatured to make it unfit for drinking by adding small amounts of:
options: A) Pure distilled water and sucrose
C) Methanol and pyridine (together with copper sulfate for colour)
D) Sodium chloride and citric acid
questions.explanation: Denatured alcohol (methylated spirit) contains poisonous methanol (~5-10%) and foul-smelling pyridine, often with copper sulfate dye to give a warning colour.

questions.topic: Unit VII: Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers
questions.question: 4-Methoxyphenol (p-methoxyphenol) is a weaker acid than phenol because:
options: A) The methoxy group has a stronger -I effect than nitro
B) 4-Methoxyphenol is completely insoluble in water
C) Phenol contains two extra hydroxyl groups
D) The methoxy group (-OCH3) donates electron density into the aromatic ring by resonance (+M effect), destabilizing the phenoxide anion
questions.explanation: Although the methoxy group has a weak -I effect, its strong +M (resonance electron-donating) effect at the para position increases electron density on the ring, destabilizing the phenoxide ion.

questions.topic: Unit VII: Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers
questions.sub_topic: Oxidation of Tertiary Alcohols with Strong Oxidants
questions.question: Tertiary alcohols resist oxidation under mild conditions because they lack an \( \alpha \)-hydrogen, but under vigorous conditions with acidified \( \ce{KMnO4} \), they:
options: A) Form tertiary aldehydes directly without carbon loss
B) Are reduced smoothly into alkanes
C) Form cyclic ethers without loss of carbon
D) Undergo dehydration to alkenes followed by oxidative cleavage into a mixture of carboxylic acids with fewer carbon atoms
questions.explanation: Under vigorous acidic oxidizing conditions, tertiary alcohols dehydrate to alkenes, which then undergo C-C bond cleavage to yield a mixture of carboxylic acids having fewer carbons than the substrate.

questions.topic: Unit VII: Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers
questions.sub_topic: Williamson Synthesis Limitations with Tertiary Alkyl Halides
questions.question: If tert-butyl bromide is treated with sodium ethoxide in ethanol, the major product obtained is:
options: A) tert-Butyl ethyl ether via substitution
questions.explanation: Sodium ethoxide is both a strong nucleophile and a strong base. With a bulky tertiary alkyl halide, elimination (E2) completely outcompetes substitution, yielding 2-methylpropene.

questions.topic: Unit VII: Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers
questions.sub_topic: Cleavage of Unsymmetrical Ethers with Cold HI
questions.question: When ethyl isopropyl ether is treated with one equivalent of cold concentrated HI, the products formed are:
options: B) Ethyl iodide and isopropyl iodide
questions.explanation: When both alkyl groups are primary or secondary, reaction proceeds via \( \text{S}_\text{N}2 \). The nucleophile \( \ce{I^-} \) attacks the less sterically hindered primary carbon (ethyl group), forming ethyl iodide and propan-2-ol.

questions.topic: Unit VIII: Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids
questions.sub_topic: Oxidation of Methyl Ketones with Sodium Hypohalite
questions.question: The haloform reaction of a methyl ketone (\( \ce{R-CO-CH3} \)) with sodium hypohalite (\( \ce{NaOX} \)) yields a haloform (\( \ce{CHX3} \)) and:
options: A) A sodium carboxylate salt having one carbon atom less than the parent ketone
B) A carboxylic acid having one carbon atom more than the parent ketone
C) A primary alcohol and carbon dioxide
D) An alkane having the same number of carbon atoms
questions.explanation: \( \ce{R-CO-CH3 + 3NaOX -> R-COONa + CHX3 + 2NaOH} \). The methyl group is cleaved as haloform, leaving the carboxylate salt \( \ce{R-COONa} \).

questions.topic: Unit VIII: Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids
questions.question: The reaction of an aldehyde or ketone with hydroxylamine (\( \ce{NH2OH} \)) produces an:
questions.explanation: \( \ce{>C=O + H2N-OH -> >C=N-OH + H2O} \). Nucleophilic addition of hydroxylamine followed by dehydration gives an oxime.

questions.topic: Unit VIII: Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids
questions.sub_topic: Relative Acidity of Benzoic Acid Derivatives
questions.question: What is the correct decreasing order of acidic strength among the following carboxylic acids?
questions.explanation: Electron-withdrawing nitro group (-M, -I) stabilizes the carboxylate anion, increasing acidity. Electron-donating methoxy group (+M) destabilizes the anion, decreasing acidity.

questions.topic: Unit VIII: Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids
questions.question: An aldehyde treated with one equivalent of monohydric alcohol in the presence of dry \( \ce{HCl} \) gas yields a hemiacetal, which on treatment with a second equivalent of alcohol yields:
options: D) A gem-dialkoxy compound known as an acetal
questions.explanation: \( \ce{R-CHO + R'OH <=>[HCl] R-CH(OH)(OR') ->[R'OH, HCl] R-CH(OR')2 + H2O} \) (acetal, a gem-diether derivative).

questions.topic: Unit VIII: Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids
questions.question: In a crossed Cannizzaro reaction between benzaldehyde and formaldehyde in concentrated \( \ce{NaOH} \), the products obtained are:
options: A) Benzyl alcohol and sodium formate
C) An equimolar mixture of benzoic acid and formic acid
questions.explanation: Formaldehyde is more susceptible to nucleophilic attack by \( \ce{OH^-} \) than benzaldehyde due to lack of steric hindrance, so formaldehyde is preferentially oxidized to formate while benzaldehyde is reduced to benzyl alcohol.

questions.question: Lower aliphatic amines (such as methylamine and ethylamine) are readily soluble in water because:
options: A) They can form intermolecular hydrogen bonds with water molecules
B) They react violently with water to form explosive gases
C) They have zero molecular dipole moment
D) They exist as metallic ions in aqueous solution
questions.explanation: The electronegative nitrogen atom and polar N-H bonds allow lower amines to engage in hydrogen bonding with water molecules, conferring high water solubility.

questions.sub_topic: Basicity of Ethyl-Substituted Amines in Aqueous Solution
questions.question: In aqueous medium, the experimentally observed order of basic strength for ethyl-substituted amines and ammonia is:
questions.explanation: For ethyl groups in aqueous solution, the balanced interplay of inductive effect, steric hindrance, and hydration of conjugate cations produces the order 2° > 3° > 1° > \( \ce{NH3} \).

questions.sub_topic: Preparation of Pure Primary Amines via Gabriel Synthesis
questions.question: Why is Gabriel phthalimide synthesis preferred over Hoffmann ammonolysis for preparing primary aliphatic amines?
options: A) It produces exclusively pure primary amines free from secondary and tertiary amine impurities
B) It produces primary amines with twice the number of carbons
C) It works with aryl halides under mild conditions
D) It does not require any heating or solvent
questions.explanation: Hoffmann ammonolysis gives a difficult-to-separate mixture of 1°, 2°, 3° amines and quaternary ammonium salts, whereas Gabriel synthesis yields uncontaminated 1° aliphatic amines.

questions.question: When a tertiary amine is treated with benzenesulfonyl chloride (Hinsberg's reagent):
options: A) No reaction occurs because tertiary amines do not contain any replaceable hydrogen atom on nitrogen
B) A clear water-soluble sulfonamide is formed instantly
C) An insoluble white precipitate of nitrobenzene is formed
D) Nitrogen gas is evolved with vigorous effervescence
questions.explanation: Tertiary amines have no hydrogen on the nitrogen atom (\( \ce{R3N} \)), so they cannot form a sulfonamide bond with benzenesulfonyl chloride and remain unreacted.

questions.sub_topic: Synthetic Applications of Diazonium: Preparation of Iodobenzene
questions.question: Iodobenzene is prepared smoothly from benzenediazonium chloride by warming with aqueous:
options: B) Potassium iodide (KI) solution without requiring any cuprous halide catalyst
C) Iodine crystals in boiling concentrated nitric acid
D) Sodium hypoiodite in dry ether
questions.explanation: Unlike Sandmeyer chlorination/bromination, the introduction of iodine does not require a copper catalyst; simply warming \( \ce{ArN2+Cl-} \) with aqueous \( \ce{KI} \) smoothly yields iodobenzene and \( \ce{N2} \).

questions.question: The cyclic stereoisomers of D-glucose (\( \alpha \)-D-glucopyranose and \( \beta \)-D-glucopyranose) that differ only in the spatial configuration at C-1 are called:
questions.explanation: Anomers are diastereomers of cyclic sugars that differ only in configuration at the hemiacetal/hemiketal carbon (C-1 in aldoses, C-2 in ketoses), known as the anomeric carbon.

questions.sub_topic: Classification of Amino Acids: Acidic vs Basic
questions.question: Which of the following amino acids contains more carboxyl groups than amino groups and is classified as an acidic amino acid?
questions.explanation: Aspartic acid (and glutamic acid) contains two \( \ce{-COOH} \) groups and one \( \ce{-NH2} \) group, making its aqueous solution acidic.

questions.question: Amylose, the water-soluble component of starch, constitutes 15–20% of starch and consists of:
options: A) A highly branched polymer held together by \( \beta \)-(1,6)-linkages
C) A cyclic heptasaccharide forming an inclusion complex
D) An unbranched long chain of 200–1000 \( \alpha \)-D-glucose units held together exclusively by \( \alpha \)-(1,4)-glycosidic linkages
questions.explanation: Amylose is a linear, unbranched helical polymer of \( \alpha \)-D-glucose connected solely by \( \alpha \)-(1,4) glycosidic bonds.

questions.question: Cellulose is a linear polysaccharide composed of which repeating unit and linkage?
questions.explanation: Cellulose is an unbranched polymer consisting exclusively of \( \beta \)-D-glucose units connected by \( \beta \)-(1,4)-glycosidic bonds, forming rigid linear chains held by inter-chain hydrogen bonds.

questions.question: The structural difference between a nucleoside and a nucleotide is that a nucleotide possesses an additional:
options: A) Amino acid attached via a peptide bond
B) Second nitrogenous base attached at C-3'
C) Phosphate group esterified at the 5'-hydroxyl position of the pentose sugar
D) Glycerol molecule attached via an ether linkage
questions.explanation: A nucleoside contains only a nitrogenous base and a pentose sugar. When the 5'-OH of the sugar is esterified with phosphoric acid, it becomes a nucleotide.
